name: Skill skeleton and SKILL.md router
description: built: skills/twm-presentation-builder/ with valid frontmatter (name = folder; description ≤1,024 chars that triggers on requests to build HTML slides/decks/presentations), SKILL.md ≤250 lines linking every part one hop away with when-to-read; no path leaves the folder; .claude/skills symlink for local trial · why: portable, discoverable, progressive disclosure · not-built: plugin packaging, hooks

name: Architecture contract and core engine
description: built: ARCHITECTURE part documenting layer order, data-attribute authoring contract, component API and shared SVG defs; core engine (nav, title bar/agenda, steps, overlays, notes, ambient) and a deck skeleton extracted from deck-v2, working with any slides between SLIDES markers · why: one stable contract every design layer styles · not-built: incident-specific behaviour

name: Optional engine modules
description: built: persistent scene/camera (world), narration tiles, pop-overs and tile row as optional modules, each documented with its attributes; a deck that declares none carries none · why: keep the core lean while keeping the HF deck's signature behaviours reusable · not-built: new module designs

name: Layout/components design layer
description: built: LAYOUT part + component CSS for the core components (header, nav, title/lead, columns, diagram kit, overlays, notes UI, ambient) and the optional modules (scene, narration tiles, pop-overs, tile row), reading only sys/comp tokens, lint-checked, matching the reference deck's computed styles · why: swap layout independently of colour and material · not-built: alternative component sets

name: Palette and style tokens + generator
description: built: palette and style as DTCG 2025.10 token files (ref→sys→comp); each colour role carries its usage rule and PPTX slot; each style effect declares native/approximated/lost for PPTX; a Python generator emits the CSS theme blocks and PPTX clrScheme/fontScheme; contrast gate over declared pairs per palette · why: one source, two outputs, enforceable rules · not-built: Node tooling

name: Assemble and theme-swap tool
description: built: a script that builds a new single-file deck from the skeleton with a chosen layout/palette/style and embedded fonts, and on re-run swaps only the theme blocks of an existing deck, leaving slides byte-identical; output is offline and endpoint-safe · why: design interchangeable without touching content · not-built: a viewing build step

name: Editorial theme from HF deck
description: built: the HF deck's palette (paper, charcoal, single green accent) and editorial style (Newsreader/Inter, bokeh, frost, line-drawn diagrams) as the default theme; a skill-built HF slide subset matches deck-v2's look at the review sizes, incl. the opaque shadowed pop-over tile · why: proven default and gold reference · not-built: brand naming of the accent

name: Second palette (blind-evaluated)
description: built: a contrasting palette (colour scheme only: four bright primaries on white, PRD Decisions) over the same components and editorial style, passing the contrast gate and judged by the eval's subagents only · why: proves the palette layer swaps cleanly · not-built: style or component changes, prototypes, presenter verdict (deferred)

name: Generic deck tools
description: built: shoot (every slide × step × review size), layout guard (overlap/overflow/off-canvas per step and size) and font embedding, each taking any deck path and configurable sizes, runnable via uv · why: the screenshot and layout gates work for any deck · not-built: HF-specific content checks

name: Process part
description: built: PROCESS part plus an AGENTS.md template the skill installs into the deck project (CLAUDE.md = @AGENTS.md): PRD → one-question interview → research with consent → prototype or recorded in-situ choice → spec → TDD red/green → look at assembled screenshots → done; PRD/SPEC templates and the HF deck's lessons · why: the dev approach persists across sessions · not-built: hooks or other enforcement (the eval measures compliance)

name: Content/storyboard part
description: built: storyboard method and template (core message codes, chapters, timings, per-slide visual, overlays, sources, message served) · why: content swappable without touching design · not-built: topic-specific content

name: Research part
description: built: sourcing method, research index and note templates, citation and flagging rules (single-sourced, disputed, paraphrase), verbatim-quote handling · why: every claim traceable · not-built: research automation

name: Voice part and personal profile
description: built: voice contract (how a profile is applied and extended with verdicts) and the presenter's profile from docs/VOICE.md (rules + approved/rejected pairs) · why: copy sounds like the presenter · not-built: generic or other voices

name: HF incident worked example
description: built: examples/hf-incident with cited excerpts (PRD, storyboard rows, voice pairs, design decisions, an ADR) and assembled screenshots, plus the v2 first-draft failure and its fix, each linked from the part it illustrates · why: agents learn from a real case · not-built: the full deck or research corpus

name: Criterion library
description: built: every criterion defined once (id, concern, evidence type D/S/T, binary item or fully described 0–5 scale, anchors, flaw taxonomy refs) across content, research, voice, design layers, architecture, PPTX and process · why: DRY rubric reused by all profiles · not-built: weights (profiles own them)

name: Deck-type profiles
description: built: editorial-talk, pitch, data-review and internal-update profiles that select and weight criteria by id, declare gates and add only profile-specific criteria; an unknown criterion id fails · why: one library adapts to deck types · not-built: handout profile

name: Deterministic gates
description: built: a runner for every D criterion on a deck (layout, contrast, offline/endpoint-safe, unique titles, alt text, word density, reachable steps), on its PPTX (through the PPTX part's own checks) and on a repo (red commit before build commit, tests fail at red, index row with doc change, screenshots before done) emitting verdicts in the judge format · why: code checks what code can · not-built: judgement calls

name: Eval protocol and judge prompts
description: built: EVAL part with the scope prompt (target, concerns, output/process, depth, transcripts only on approval), judge prompts for generic subagents (isolated criterion, artefact-only context, evidence→rationale→score JSON, insufficient-evidence, k repeats, median, spread flag, pointwise; pairwise both orders for A/B), dated result files and a report that states calibration status · why: rigorous, repeatable judging · not-built: API runner

name: Bundled test briefs
description: built: four briefs (HF subset with gold reference, same subset in the second palette, synthetic pitch, synthetic data review), each with profile, fixed research pack and expected features · why: repeatable iteration on the skill · not-built: real-topic briefs

name: Flawed anchor decks
description: built: deliberately broken variants (collisions, contrast, hook titles, unsourced claims, restated step lists, the v2 first-draft faults) each labelled with the criteria it must fail; judges and gates are expected to fail them · why: anchors without a calibration set; catches lenient judges · not-built: presenter-scored calibration

name: Feature coverage check
description: built: a feature list of the skill mapped to briefs and criteria; a check fails when any feature lacks a brief and a criterion · why: new features can't land without eval coverage · not-built: coverage of excluded features

name: PPTX animation spike
description: built: entrance, exit, emphasis and motion-path animations in step order written as PPTX timing XML, round-tripping through python-pptx, schema-valid, and playing correctly in PowerPoint (presenter-confirmed, 23 Nov) · why: riskiest PPTX unknown, settled first · not-built: Morph, full emitter

name: PPTX scene extraction
description: built: browser measurement of every slide's final state and per-step deltas into a scene (component role, geometry, text runs, token colours, SVG primitives, notes) · why: geometry from the real render · not-built: emitting PPTX

name: PPTX emitter
description: built: one editable slide per HTML slide from a seed template per theme: layouts with placeholders, theme colours/fonts from tokens, named native shapes/freeforms/connectors (SVG+PNG fallback otherwise), speaker notes, steps as animations (Morph only where none fits), effects per the style's bands; validates, re-flows into a foreign template, and text wrap is judged visually against the HTML (no numeric tolerance) · why: editable hand-off · not-built: pixel fidelity

name: Eval run tooling
description: built: shipped tools for what a run needs beyond gates and aggregation: per-slide text extracts for text judges, contact sheets so deck-scope judges see every state, anchor judge-accuracy tables, several decks in one run folder without verdict collisions, and an explicit missing reason when a PPTX renderer is absent · why: the baseline run had to improvise these · not-built: an API judge runner

name: Baseline eval run and acceptance
description: built: a full eval over all briefs and anchors with a dated report; anchors fail as labelled; presenter reviews the report and HF example screenshots · why: proves the skill end to end · not-built: calibration against presenter scores
